index.subtitle: High School Student | Mathematics Enthusiast | Also a sprinter :)
paragraphs: Hello! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from Canada with a strong interest in pure mathematics.

My primary interests include algebra, algebraic number theory, commutative algebra, and arithmetic geometry. This website documents my learning, research projects, expository writing, and mathematical notes.
Outside Mathematics, I am a sprinter and enjoy track and field. I also have some interest in computer science, though not as much as mathematics :)

Hello! I'm Kasieobi Udumaga, a high school student from Canada with a strong passion for pure mathematics. I've been fascinated by numbers, patterns, and mathematical structures since the first grade, and I'm particularly drawn to the beauty and depth of algebraic number theory and commutative algebra.
My goal is to pursue a career in mathematics research and contribute to the field through original work and expository writing.
I'm always happy to connect with fellow mathematics enthusiasts. Please feel free to reach out via the contact page.

contact.subtitle: I'd love to hear from you. Whether you have a question about mathematics, feedback on my notes, or just want to say hello — feel free to reach out.

welcome.heading: Get in Touch
paragraphs: I'm always happy to connect with fellow mathematics enthusiasts, students, and researchers. Whether you'd like to discuss a mathematical idea, ask about my notes, share feedback on the website, or explore potential collaborations — please don't hesitate to write.
I do my best to respond to all messages, though it may take me a few days during busy periods.

notes.intro: Welcome to my collection of mathematical notes. This page is a growing library of notes that I have written while learning and exploring different areas of mathematics, ranging from olympiad topics to undergraduate and graduate subjects. Mathematics is best understood through examples, proofs, problem solving, and revisiting ideas over time, and these notes reflect that process. Most of these notes are living documents that will continue to be refined and expanded as I learn more. I hope they are useful to students, problem solvers, and anyone with an interest in mathematics, and that they encourage others to explore the beauty, creativity, and depth of the subject.
